records.source: וַיִּסְעוּ֙ מֵֽאֵילִ֔ם וַיָּבֹ֜אוּ כָּל־עֲדַ֤ת בְּנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אֶל־מִדְבַּר־סִ֔ין אֲשֶׁ֥ר בֵּין־אֵילִ֖ם וּבֵ֣ין סִינָ֑י בַּחֲמִשָּׁ֨ה עָשָׂ֥ר יוֹם֙ לַחֹ֣דֶשׁ הַשֵּׁנִ֔י לְצֵאתָ֖ם מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: And they set out from Elim, and came all [the] congregation of [the] sons of Israel to [the] wilderness of Sin, which [is] between Elim and Sinai, on [the] fifteenth day of the second month of their going out from [the] land of Egypt.
pieces: After leaving Elim, the whole community of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} arrived in the wilderness of Sin, between Elim and Sinai. It was the fifteenth day of the second month since they had come out of the land of Egypt.

L.1: And they set out from Elim, and all the congregation of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel came to the wilderness of Sin, which [is] between Elim and Sinai, on the fifteenth day of the second month of their going out from the land of Egypt.

R.1: The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} left Elim and came to the Desert of Sin, which lies between Elim and Mount Sinai. It was the fifteenth day of the second month after they left Egypt.

decisions.choice: the wilderness of Sin: a place name
decisions.reason: Sin is the name of a stretch of wilderness on the way to Sinai (17:1; Numbers 33:11-12). The name has nothing to do with wrongdoing; it may be related to the name Sinai.

decisions.choice: the fifteenth day of the second month: one month after leaving Egypt
decisions.reason: Israel left Egypt on the fifteenth day of the first month, the day after the Passover (12:6, 18; Numbers 33:3). So a month has passed since the exodus.

decisions.choice: Mount Sinai
decisions.reason: Readable says "Mount Sinai", the mountain where Israel will camp in chapter 19, so that the reader knows what Sinai is.

records.heading: The people grumble for food

records.source: וַיִּלּ֜וֹנוּ כָּל־עֲדַ֧ת בְּנֵי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל עַל־מֹשֶׁ֥ה וְעַֽל־אַהֲרֹ֖ן בַּמִּדְבָּֽר׃
records.gloss: And grumbled all [the] congregation of [the] sons of Israel against Moses and against Aaron in the wilderness.
pieces: There in the wilderness the whole community of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} grumbled against Moses and Aaron.

L.2: And all the congregation of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel grumbled against Moses and against Aaron in the wilderness.

R.2: Out in the desert, all the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} complained about Moses and Aaron.

decisions.choice: grumbled: complained with resentment
decisions.reason: The verb means to murmur or complain against someone, with distrust behind it. Israel grumbled at Marah (15:24), and will again at Rephidim (17:3) and many times in the wilderness (Numbers 14:2, 27). The word and the noun from it run through this chapter (verses 7-9, 12).

decisions.choice: complained
decisions.reason: Readable uses the common word "complain" for this verb throughout the chapter; Literal and Balanced say "grumble".

records.source: וַיֹּאמְר֨וּ אֲלֵהֶ֜ם בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל מִֽי־יִתֵּ֨ן מוּתֵ֤נוּ בְיַד־יְהוָה֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם בְּשִׁבְתֵּ֨נוּ֙ עַל־סִ֣יר הַבָּשָׂ֔ר בְּאָכְלֵ֥נוּ לֶ֖חֶם לָשֹׂ֑בַע כִּֽי־הוֹצֵאתֶ֤ם אֹתָ֨נוּ֙ אֶל־הַמִּדְבָּ֣ר הַזֶּ֔ה לְהָמִ֛ית אֶת־כָּל־הַקָּהָ֥ל הַזֶּ֖ה בָּרָעָֽב׃ס
records.gloss: And said to them [the] sons of Israel, who will give [that] we died by [the] hand of Yahweh in [the] land of Egypt, when we sat by [the] pot of the meat, when we ate bread to fullness; for you have brought out us into the wilderness this to kill all the assembly this by hunger.
pieces: The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} said to them, "We wish we had died at the hand of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in the land of Egypt! There we sat beside the pots of meat and ate all the bread we could hold. But you two have brought us out into this wilderness to make this whole assembly die of hunger."

L.3: And the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel said to them, "Who would grant that we had died by the hand of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in the land of Egypt, when we sat by the pot of meat, when we ate bread to the full! For you have brought us out into this wilderness to kill this whole assembly with hunger."

R.3: They told Moses and Aaron, "It would have been better for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to put us to death in Egypt! There we had pots of meat to sit beside, and we ate bread until we were full. Now you have led us out into this desert to make this whole crowd starve."

decisions.choice: who will give ...: an exclamation of wish, if only
decisions.reason: "Who will give" is a set way of wishing for something (16:3; Numbers 11:29; 14:2; Deuteronomy 28:67). It asks no real question.

decisions.choice: died by the hand of Yahweh in Egypt: died in the plagues as the Egyptians did
decisions.reason: "The hand of Yahweh" brought the plagues on Egypt (9:3) and the death of the firstborn. The people say they would rather have died there, with full stomachs, than starve in the wilderness.

decisions.choice: the pot of meat ... bread to the full: plenty of food
decisions.reason: The pot is a cooking pot for boiling meat; "bread" often means food in general. Looking back, the people remember Egypt as a place of plenty, though they were slaves there (1:13-14; 2:23). They speak of the pot in the singular, the cooking pot of each household.

decisions.choice: you two / Moses and Aaron
decisions.reason: "You" is plural, Moses and Aaron (verse 2). Balanced says "you two"; Readable names them at the start.

records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֔ה הִנְנִ֨י מַמְטִ֥יר לָכֶ֛ם לֶ֖חֶם מִן־הַשָּׁמָ֑יִם וְיָצָ֨א הָעָ֤ם וְלָֽקְטוּ֙ דְּבַר־י֣וֹם בְּיוֹמ֔וֹ לְמַ֧עַן אֲנַסֶּ֛נּוּ הֲיֵלֵ֥ךְ בְּתוֹרָתִ֖י אִם־לֹֽא׃
records.gloss: And said Yahweh to Moses, here I [am] about to rain for you bread from the heavens, and will go out the people and they will gather [the] matter of a day in its day, so that I may test it, whether it will walk in my law or not.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "I am about to rain bread from heaven for you. Each day the people are to go out and gather the amount needed for that day. By this I will test them, to see whether they will live by {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} law or not.

L.4: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Behold, I am about to rain bread from heaven for you, and the people shall go out and gather a day's matter in its day, that I may test them, whether they will walk in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} law or not.

R.4: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "I am going to send bread down like rain from the sky for you. Every day the people must go out and gather enough for that one day. This will test them, to show if they will obey {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} law.

decisions.choice: rain bread from heaven: food sent down from God
decisions.reason: God will send food down from the sky as he sends rain. The word for heaven is also the word for sky. Psalm 78:24 and 105:40 call the manna "grain of heaven" and "bread of heaven", and Jesus takes up this verse in John 6:31-32.

decisions.choice: a day's matter in its day: each day's portion on its day
decisions.reason: The phrase means the amount a day requires, gathered on that day. It is the rule the people are tested by: they must trust God for tomorrow's food (verses 19-20).

decisions.choice: that I may test them, whether they will walk in my law: the gift is also a test
decisions.reason: To test is to prove what is in someone, as at Marah (15:25) and later in Deuteronomy 8:2-3, 16, which looks back on the manna. To walk in God's law is to live by his instruction; here that instruction is the rule about gathering and the Sabbath (verses 5, 26-28).

decisions.choice: live by
decisions.reason: "Walk in" is a picture of how one lives. Literal keeps "walk in"; Balanced says "live by"; Readable says "obey".

records.source: וְהָיָה֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשִּׁשִּׁ֔י וְהֵכִ֖ינוּ אֵ֣ת אֲשֶׁר־יָבִ֑יאוּ וְהָיָ֣ה מִשְׁנֶ֔ה עַ֥ל אֲשֶֽׁר־יִלְקְט֖וּ י֥וֹם׀יֽוֹם׃ס
records.gloss: And it will be on the sixth day, and they will prepare what they bring in, and it will be double over what they gather day [by] day.
pieces: When they prepare on the sixth day what they have brought in, it will amount to double their usual daily gathering."

L.5: And it shall be on the sixth day, they shall prepare what they bring in, and it shall be double over what they gather day by day."

R.5: On the sixth day, when they get ready the food they bring in, they will find there is twice as much as on the other days."

decisions.choice: it will be double: the sixth day's portion will be twice the daily one
alternatives: they are to gather twice as much
decisions.reason: The verse does not say whether God will make the gathering double or whether the people are to gather double. Verse 22 says they gathered twice as much, and verse 29 says that God gives bread for two days on the sixth day. Both are true: the people gather, and God provides.

decisions.choice: prepare: get ready, cook
decisions.reason: To prepare is to make the food ready to eat or keep; verse 23 explains it as baking and boiling.

decisions.choice: they will find
decisions.reason: Readable adds "they will find" so that the double portion is shown as something that happens to them, without deciding how (see m1).

records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר מֹשֶׁה֙ וְאַהֲרֹ֔ן אֶֽל־כָּל־בְּנֵ֖י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל עֶ֕רֶב וִֽידַעְתֶּ֕ם כִּ֧י יְהוָ֛ה הוֹצִ֥יא אֶתְכֶ֖ם מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: And said Moses and Aaron to all [the] sons of Israel, evening, and you will know that Yahweh brought out you from [the] land of Egypt.
pieces: Moses and Aaron told all the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, "This evening you will come to know that it was {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} who led you out of the land of Egypt,

L.6: And Moses and Aaron said to all the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, "[At] evening you will know that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} brought you out from the land of Egypt,

R.6: Moses and Aaron said to all the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, "Tonight you will find out that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is the one who brought you out of Egypt.

decisions.choice: you will know that Yahweh brought you out: not Moses and Aaron
decisions.reason: The people had said that Moses and Aaron brought them out to die (verse 3). Moses and Aaron answer that the evening's gift will show who really brought them out. "You will know" echoes God's purpose in the plagues (6:7; 7:5).

decisions.choice: evening: this evening, when the meat comes
decisions.reason: "Evening" stands first without a preposition, meaning "in the evening". It points to the quail of verse 13, as "morning" in verse 7 points to the bread.

decisions.choice: it was ... who
decisions.reason: Balanced stresses "the LORD" to bring out the contrast with "you" (Moses and Aaron) in verse 3; Readable does the same with "is the one who".

records.source: וּבֹ֗קֶר וּרְאִיתֶם֙ אֶת־כְּב֣וֹד יְהוָ֔ה בְּשָׁמְע֥וֹ אֶת־תְּלֻנֹּתֵיכֶ֖ם עַל־יְהוָ֑ה וְנַ֣חְנוּ מָ֔ה כִּ֥י תַלִּ֖ינוּ עָלֵֽינוּ׃
records.gloss: And morning, and you will see the glory of Yahweh, in his hearing your grumblings against Yahweh; and we, what [are we], that you grumble against us?
pieces: and in the morning you will see the glory of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. For {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has heard the grumbling you have aimed at {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. As for us, what are we? Why grumble against us?"

L.7: and [in the] morning you will see the glory of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hearing your grumblings against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. And we, what [are we], that you grumble against us?"

R.7: In the morning you will see the glory of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. He has heard you complaining against {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. We are only men. Why do you complain about us?"

decisions.choice: the glory of Yahweh: the shining presence of God made visible
decisions.reason: God's glory is his weight and splendor, made visible to people. In verse 10 it appears in the cloud. Seeing it in the morning may also mean seeing God's power in the bread he sends (verses 13-15).

decisions.choice: in his hearing: because he has heard
decisions.reason: The phrase gives the reason God will show himself: he has heard the people's grumbling. Grumbling against God's servants is grumbling against God (verse 8).

decisions.choice: what are we: we are nothing
decisions.reason: The question means that Moses and Aaron are of no account in this; the people's quarrel is with God, not with them (verse 8; Numbers 16:11).

decisions.choice: We are only men.
decisions.reason: Readable turns the question "what are we?" into the statement it implies.

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֗ה בְּתֵ֣ת יְהוָה֩ לָכֶ֨ם בָּעֶ֜רֶב בָּשָׂ֣ר לֶאֱכֹ֗ל וְלֶ֤חֶם בַּבֹּ֨קֶר֙ לִשְׂבֹּ֔עַ בִּשְׁמֹ֤עַ יְהוָה֙ אֶת־תְּלֻנֹּ֣תֵיכֶ֔ם אֲשֶׁר־אַתֶּ֥ם מַלִּינִ֖ם עָלָ֑יו וְנַ֣חְנוּ מָ֔ה לֹא־עָלֵ֥ינוּ תְלֻנֹּתֵיכֶ֖ם כִּ֥י עַל־יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And said Moses, in [the] giving of Yahweh to you in the evening meat to eat and bread in the morning to be satisfied, in [the] hearing of Yahweh your grumblings that you grumble against him; and we, what [are we]? Not against us [are] your grumblings, but against Yahweh.
pieces: Moses went on, "You will see this when {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gives you meat to eat in the evening, and bread in the morning until you are full, because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has heard the grumbling you direct at {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. What are we? Your grumbling is not aimed at us at all, but at {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."

L.8: And Moses said, "[This will be] when {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gives you in the evening meat to eat and in the morning bread to the full, when {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} hears your grumblings that you grumble against {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. And we, what [are we]? Your grumblings [are] not against us but against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."

R.8: Moses said, "In the evening {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will give you meat to eat. In the morning {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will give you all the bread you can eat. He has heard you complaining about {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. Who are we? When you complain, it is really {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} you are complaining about, not us."

decisions.choice: in the giving: when Yahweh gives, you will know
alternatives: Yahweh will give you meat in the evening
decisions.reason: The sentence begins with "when Yahweh gives" and never finishes the thought. It takes up verses 6-7: the people will know and see Yahweh when he gives meat in the evening and bread in the morning.

decisions.choice: not against us but against Yahweh: to grumble against God's messengers is to grumble against God
decisions.reason: Moses and Aaron are only servants carrying out God's word, so the complaint reaches God himself (compare 1 Samuel 8:7).

decisions.choice: You will see this when (Balanced); In the evening ... will give (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced supplies the unfinished thought from verses 6-7. Readable turns the clause into plain statements of what God will do.

records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר מֹשֶׁה֙ אֶֽל־אַהֲרֹ֔ן אֱמֹ֗ר אֶֽל־כָּל־עֲדַת֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל קִרְב֖וּ לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה כִּ֣י שָׁמַ֔ע אֵ֖ת תְּלֻנֹּתֵיכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And said Moses to Aaron, say to all [the] congregation of [the] sons of Israel, come near before Yahweh, for he has heard your grumblings.
pieces: Moses told Aaron to tell the whole community of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} to come close and stand before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had heard their grumbling.

L.9: And Moses said to Aaron, "Say to all the congregation of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, 'Come near before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, for {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has heard your grumblings.'"

R.9: Moses told Aaron to say to all the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, "Come and stand in front of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. He has heard your complaints."

decisions.choice: come near before Yahweh: gather in God's presence
decisions.reason: The people are called to stand before God as before a judge or king. Verse 10 shows his presence in the cloud.

decisions.choice: indirect speech
decisions.reason: Balanced reports Moses' words to Aaron as indirect speech to avoid a quotation inside a quotation. The meaning is unchanged.

records.source: וַיְהִ֗י כְּדַבֵּ֤ר אַהֲרֹן֙ אֶל־כָּל־עֲדַ֣ת בְּנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיִּפְנ֖וּ אֶל־הַמִּדְבָּ֑ר וְהִנֵּה֙ כְּב֣וֹד יְהוָ֔ה נִרְאָ֖ה בֶּעָנָֽן׃פ
records.gloss: And it was as Aaron spoke to all [the] congregation of [the] sons of Israel, and they turned to the wilderness, and behold, [the] glory of Yahweh appeared in the cloud.
pieces: While Aaron was still addressing the whole community of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, they turned to face the wilderness, and suddenly the glory of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} could be seen in the cloud.

L.10: And it came about, as Aaron spoke to all the congregation of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, that they turned toward the wilderness, and behold, the glory of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} appeared in the cloud.

R.10: While Aaron was speaking to all the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, they looked out toward the desert. There they saw the glory of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} shining in the cloud.

decisions.choice: the cloud: the pillar of cloud that led Israel
decisions.reason: The article points to a known cloud: the pillar of cloud that went before Israel (13:21-22; 14:19-20). God's glory is seen in it again at Sinai (24:15-17) and at the tabernacle (40:34-35).

decisions.choice: behold: a sudden sight
decisions.reason: The word draws attention to what the people suddenly saw, from their point of view.

decisions.choice: shining
decisions.reason: Readable says the glory was "shining" in the cloud, since God's glory is a visible brightness (24:17). "Appeared" is the Hebrew verb.

records.source: וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֥ה לֵּאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And spoke Yahweh to Moses, saying,
pieces: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses,

L.11: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses, saying,

decisions.choice: spoke ... saying: the formula that introduces God's words
decisions.reason: The same formula opens God's speeches in 6:10, 13:1 and 14:1. The words follow in verse 12.

records.heading: Quail and bread from heaven

records.source: שָׁמַ֗עְתִּי אֶת־תְּלוּנֹּת֮ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵל֒ דַּבֵּ֨ר אֲלֵהֶ֜ם לֵאמֹ֗ר בֵּ֤ין הָֽעַרְבַּ֨יִם֙ תֹּאכְל֣וּ בָשָׂ֔ר וּבַבֹּ֖קֶר תִּשְׂבְּעוּ־לָ֑חֶם וִֽידַעְתֶּ֕ם כִּ֛י אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: I have heard the grumblings of [the] sons of Israel. Speak to them, saying, between the evenings you will eat meat, and in the morning you will be satisfied [with] bread, and you will know that I [am] Yahweh your God.
pieces: "The grumbling of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} has reached {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} ears. Tell them this: 'As evening falls you will eat meat, and in the morning you will have your fill of bread. Then you will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God.'"

L.12: "I have heard the grumblings of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel. Speak to them, saying, 'Between the two evenings you will eat meat, and in the morning you will be filled with bread, and you will know that I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God.'"

R.12: "I have heard the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} complaining. Tell them that at sundown they will eat meat, and in the morning they will have plenty of bread. Then they will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} their God."

decisions.choice: between the two evenings: at dusk
decisions.reason: The phrase means the time between sunset and dark, as when the Passover lamb was killed (12:6).

decisions.choice: you will know that I am Yahweh your God: the purpose of the gift
decisions.reason: God promised in 6:7 that Israel would know him as their God who brought them out of Egypt. The food in the wilderness will teach them this.

decisions.choice: has reached my ears
decisions.reason: Balanced puts "I have heard" as "has reached my ears"; the sense is the same.

decisions.choice: indirect speech
decisions.reason: Readable reports the message as indirect speech ("Tell them that ... they will") to avoid a quotation inside a quotation.

records.source: וַיְהִ֣י בָעֶ֔רֶב וַתַּ֣עַל הַשְּׂלָ֔ו וַתְּכַ֖ס אֶת־הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֑ה וּבַבֹּ֗קֶר הָֽיְתָה֙ שִׁכְבַ֣ת הַטַּ֔ל סָבִ֖יב לַֽמַּחֲנֶֽה׃
records.gloss: And it was in the evening, and came up the quail and covered the camp; and in the morning there was a layer of the dew around the camp.
pieces: That evening, quail flew in and covered the camp, and by morning dew lay all around the camp.

L.13: And it came about in the evening that the quail came up and covered the camp, and in the morning there was a layer of dew around the camp.

R.13: That evening, so many quail came that they covered the camp. In the morning, the ground all around the camp was wet with dew.

decisions.choice: quail: a small game bird
decisions.reason: Quail are small birds that fly in great numbers over the Sinai region on their yearly migration and often come down to the ground exhausted. God sends them again in Numbers 11:31-32 (see also Psalm 105:40).

decisions.choice: a layer of dew: the dew that fell with the manna
decisions.reason: Numbers 11:9 says the manna fell on the camp with the dew at night. The next verse tells what was left when the dew lifted.

decisions.choice: so many quail came
decisions.reason: Readable spells out that the camp was covered because the birds came in great numbers.

records.source: וַתַּ֖עַל שִׁכְבַ֣ת הַטָּ֑ל וְהִנֵּ֞ה עַל־פְּנֵ֤י הַמִּדְבָּר֙ דַּ֣ק מְחֻסְפָּ֔ס דַּ֥ק כַּכְּפֹ֖ר עַל־הָאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: And went up the layer of the dew, and behold, on [the] face of the wilderness, thin [stuff], flake-like, thin like the hoarfrost on the ground.
pieces: When the dew had lifted, the surface of the wilderness was covered with something fine and flaky, as thin as frost on the ground.

L.14: And the layer of dew went up, and behold, on the face of the wilderness [was something] fine, flake-like, fine as hoarfrost on the ground.

R.14: When the dew dried up, thin flakes were left lying on the desert ground. They looked like frost.

decisions.choice: flake-like: flaky, or perhaps scaly or round
decisions.reason: The word occurs only here in the Bible, so its meaning is not certain. It is usually taken to mean flaky or scale-like; some take it as round, in the way coriander seed is round (verse 31).

decisions.choice: fine ... as hoarfrost: thin and white like frost
decisions.reason: "Fine" means thin or small. Hoarfrost is the white frost that forms on the ground in a cold night (Psalm 147:16).

decisions.choice: They looked like frost.
decisions.reason: Readable splits the description into two short sentences.

records.source: וַיִּרְא֣וּ בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל וַיֹּ֨אמְר֜וּ אִ֤ישׁ אֶל־אָחִיו֙ מָ֣ן ה֔וּא כִּ֛י לֹ֥א יָדְע֖וּ מַה־ה֑וּא וַיֹּ֤אמֶר מֹשֶׁה֙ אֲלֵהֶ֔ם ה֣וּא הַלֶּ֔חֶם אֲשֶׁ֨ר נָתַ֧ן יְהוָ֛ה לָכֶ֖ם לְאָכְלָֽה׃
records.gloss: And saw [the] sons of Israel and said each to his brother, what [is] it? For not they knew what it [was]. And said Moses to them, it [is] the bread that has given Yahweh to you for food.
pieces: "What is it?" the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} asked one another when they saw it, since they did not know what it was. Moses answered them, "It is bread, given to you by {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} as your food.

L.15: And the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel saw [it], and they said one to another, "What [is] it?" for they did not know what it [was]. And Moses said to them, "It [is] the bread that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has given you for food.

R.15: When the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} saw it, they asked each other, "What is it?" They had no idea what it was. Moses told them, "This is the bread {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has given you to eat.

decisions.choice: What is it?: a word-play on the name manna
alternatives: it is manna (taking the word as the name already)
decisions.reason: The people ask "What is it?" with a rare word for "what" that sounds the same as the name the food is given in verse 31, "manna". The word appears to be an old or regional form, which the narrator explains at once with the ordinary word for "what" ("they did not know what it was"). So the name manna recalls the question: the food was named after the people's puzzlement.

decisions.choice: the bread that Yahweh has given you: the promised bread from heaven
decisions.reason: Moses names the strange flakes as the bread God promised in verse 4. Jesus takes this up in John 6:31-35.

decisions.choice: "What is it?" first
decisions.reason: Balanced puts the question first, so that the words the name comes from stand out.

records.source: זֶ֤ה הַדָּבָר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר צִוָּ֣ה יְהוָ֔ה לִקְט֣וּ מִמֶּ֔נּוּ אִ֖ישׁ לְפִ֣י אָכְל֑וֹ עֹ֣מֶר לַגֻּלְגֹּ֗לֶת מִסְפַּר֙ נַפְשֹׁ֣תֵיכֶ֔ם אִ֛ישׁ לַאֲשֶׁ֥ר בְּאָהֳל֖וֹ תִּקָּֽחוּ׃
records.gloss: This [is] the word that has commanded Yahweh: gather of it each to [the] mouth of his eating, an omer for a head, [the] number of your persons, each for [those] who [are] in his tent you will take.
pieces: Here is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has commanded: 'Each of you is to gather as much as you need to eat, {{units:about 2 quarts|an omer}} for every person. The head of each household is to collect it for everyone who lives in his tent.'"

L.16: This [is] the thing that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has commanded: 'Gather of it, {{gender:each one|each man}} according to {{gender:their|his}} eating, an omer per head, [by] the number of your persons; you shall take, each man for those in his tent.'"

R.16: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has commanded you to gather as much as you need to eat. Take {{units:about 2 quarts|an omer}} for each person. Collect it for everyone who lives in your tent."

decisions.choice: omer: a dry measure, about two quarts
decisions.reason: The omer is a measure for grain and dry food, a tenth of an ephah (verse 36). It held roughly two quarts (about two liters), a day's food for one person. The word is used for this measure only in this chapter.

decisions.choice: according to the mouth of his eating: as much as each one eats
decisions.reason: "To the mouth of" means "in proportion to". Each person is to gather what he or she needs (also verses 18 and 21).

decisions.choice: each man for those in his tent: the head of each household
decisions.reason: One person, the head of the household, gathered for everyone who lived in the family tent, an omer for each of them.

decisions.choice: {{units:about 2 quarts|an omer}}
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the modern measure, with "omer" as the reader's alternative. Literal keeps "omer".

decisions.choice: indirect speech
decisions.reason: Readable reports the command as indirect speech, since Moses is already speaking.

records.source: וַיַּעֲשׂוּ־כֵ֖ן בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַֽיִּלְקְט֔וּ הַמַּרְבֶּ֖ה וְהַמַּמְעִֽיט׃
records.gloss: And did so [the] sons of Israel, and they gathered, the [one who] made much and the [one who] made little.
pieces: The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} did this. Some of them gathered a lot, and others only a little.

L.17: And the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel did so, and they gathered, the one [gathering] much and the one [gathering] little.

R.17: The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} did what they were told. Some gathered more, and some gathered less.

decisions.choice: the one who made much and the one who made little: some gathered more than others
decisions.reason: The two words mean doing much and doing little, here gathering. Families of different sizes gathered different amounts, and some were simply more or less eager.

records.source: וַיָּמֹ֣דּוּ בָעֹ֔מֶר וְלֹ֤א הֶעְדִּיף֙ הַמַּרְבֶּ֔ה וְהַמַּמְעִ֖יט לֹ֣א הֶחְסִ֑יר אִ֥ישׁ לְפִֽי־אָכְל֖וֹ לָקָֽטוּ׃
records.gloss: And they measured [it] by [the] omer, and not had surplus the [one who] made much, and the [one who] made little not lacked; each to [the] mouth of his eating they gathered.
pieces: Yet when they measured it {{units:with a 2-quart measure|by the omer}}, the one who gathered much had nothing left over, and the one who gathered little had no shortage. All of them had gathered as much as they could eat.

L.18: And they measured [it] by the omer, and the one [gathering] much had no surplus, and the one [gathering] little had no lack; each had gathered according to his eating.

R.18: When they measured it {{units:2 quarts at a time|by the omer}}, the people who gathered a lot did not have too much. The people who gathered a little still had all they needed. Everyone had gathered as much as they could eat.

decisions.choice: no surplus ... no lack: God made the portions come out even
decisions.reason: However much each household gathered, when it was measured there was an omer for each person, no more and no less. Paul quotes this sentence in 2 Corinthians 8:15 to urge believers to share, so that no one has too much or too little.

decisions.choice: they measured it by the omer: each household's gathering was measured out
alternatives: the surplus of some was shared with those who had less
decisions.reason: The measuring was done at home or in the camp after gathering. The verse does not say whether the amounts evened out in the measuring or by sharing; the point is that everyone had enough.

decisions.choice: {{units:with a 2-quart measure|by the omer}}
decisions.reason: As in verse 16, Balanced and Readable give the modern measure first. Literal keeps "omer".

records.source: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֖ה אֲלֵהֶ֑ם אִ֕ישׁ אַל־יוֹתֵ֥ר מִמֶּ֖נּוּ עַד־בֹּֽקֶר׃
records.gloss: And said Moses to them, each not let him leave of it until morning.
pieces: Moses told them, "None of you may save any of it for the next morning."

L.19: And Moses said to them, "Let no one leave [any] of it until morning."

R.19: Moses told them, "Do not keep any of it until the next morning."

decisions.choice: let no one leave any until morning: trust God for the next day
decisions.reason: This is the test of verse 4: each day's food is gathered on its own day, and no one is to store it up against tomorrow (compare Matthew 6:11, 34).

records.source: וְלֹא־שָׁמְע֣וּ אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֗ה וַיּוֹתִ֨רוּ אֲנָשִׁ֤ים מִמֶּ֨נּוּ֙ עַד־בֹּ֔קֶר וַיָּ֥רֻם תּוֹלָעִ֖ים וַיִּבְאַ֑שׁ וַיִּקְצֹ֥ף עֲלֵהֶ֖ם מֹשֶֽׁה׃
records.gloss: And not they listened to Moses, and left over men of it until morning, and it bred worms and stank. And was angry with them Moses.
pieces: But they would not listen to Moses. Some people saved part of it until morning, and it became wormy and foul-smelling. This made Moses angry with them.

L.20: And they did not listen to Moses, and [some] people left [part] of it until morning, and it bred worms and stank. And Moses was angry with them.

R.20: But some of the people did not listen to Moses. They kept part of it until the next morning. By then it was full of worms and smelled bad. Moses was angry with them.

decisions.choice: it bred worms and stank: it rotted overnight
decisions.reason: The verb means to swarm or breed, with "worms" telling with what. The manna kept overnight was spoiled and rotten, against nature, for on the Sabbath it kept (verse 24).

decisions.choice: men: some people
decisions.reason: "Men" here means some of the people, not males only.

decisions.choice: some of the people
decisions.reason: Readable makes it clear from the start that only some did not listen, as the Hebrew shows by "[some] people" in the next clause.

records.source: וַיִּלְקְט֤וּ אֹתוֹ֙ בַּבֹּ֣קֶר בַּבֹּ֔קֶר אִ֖ישׁ כְּפִ֣י אָכְל֑וֹ וְחַ֥ם הַשֶּׁ֖מֶשׁ וְנָמָֽס׃
records.gloss: And they gathered it in the morning in the morning, each according to [the] mouth of his eating; and grew hot the sun and it melted.
pieces: So morning after morning they gathered it, everyone as much as they could eat, and when the heat of the sun came, what was left melted away.

L.21: And they gathered it morning by morning, each according to his eating; and the sun grew hot, and it melted.

R.21: Every morning each person gathered as much as they needed. When the sun became hot, the rest of it melted.

decisions.choice: in the morning in the morning: every morning
decisions.reason: Repeating a word means "each": every morning.

decisions.choice: it melted: the manna left on the ground melted
decisions.reason: What was not gathered melted in the heat of the day, so it could only be gathered early.

decisions.choice: what was left / the rest of it
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make clear that it was the manna left on the ground that melted.

records.source: וַיְהִ֣י׀בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשִּׁשִּׁ֗י לָֽקְט֥וּ לֶ֨חֶם֙ מִשְׁנֶ֔ה שְׁנֵ֥י הָעֹ֖מֶר לָאֶחָ֑ד וַיָּבֹ֨אוּ֙ כָּל־נְשִׂיאֵ֣י הָֽעֵדָ֔ה וַיַּגִּ֖ידוּ לְמֹשֶֽׁה׃
records.gloss: And it was on the sixth day they gathered bread double, two of the omer for the one; and came all [the] leaders of the congregation and told Moses.
pieces: On the sixth day they gathered a double amount of bread, {{units:about 4 quarts|two omers}} per person. All the leaders of the community came and told Moses about it.

L.22: And it came about on the sixth day [that] they gathered double bread, two omers for each one, and all the leaders of the congregation came and told Moses.

R.22: On the sixth day they gathered twice as much food, {{units:about 4 quarts|two omers}} for each person. All the leaders of the community came and told Moses what had happened.

decisions.choice: came and told Moses: the leaders report the double portion
alternatives: they came to complain that people had gathered too much
decisions.reason: The verse does not say why the leaders came. They may have been puzzled by the double amount, since the people had not yet been told about the Sabbath (God had told Moses in verse 5), or they may have been asking what to do with it. Moses' answer in verse 23 explains it.

decisions.choice: leaders: chiefs of the community
decisions.reason: The word means one lifted up, a chief or leader, here the heads of the tribes or clans (Numbers 1:16).

decisions.choice: {{units:about 4 quarts|two omers}}
decisions.reason: As in verse 16, the modern measure comes first, with "omers" as the alternative. Literal keeps "omers".

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲלֵהֶ֗ם ה֚וּא אֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבֶּ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה שַׁבָּת֧וֹן שַׁבַּת־קֹ֛דֶשׁ לַֽיהוָ֖ה מָחָ֑ר אֵ֣ת אֲשֶׁר־תֹּאפ֞וּ אֵפ֗וּ וְאֵ֤ת אֲשֶֽׁר־תְּבַשְּׁלוּ֙ בַּשֵּׁ֔לוּ וְאֵת֙ כָּל־הָ֣עֹדֵ֔ף הַנִּ֧יחוּ לָכֶ֛ם לְמִשְׁמֶ֖רֶת עַד־הַבֹּֽקֶר׃
records.gloss: And he said to them, it [is] what has spoken Yahweh: a sabbath observance, a sabbath of holiness to Yahweh [is] tomorrow. What you will bake, bake, and what you will boil, boil, and all the surplus leave for yourselves for keeping until the morning.
pieces: He told them, "This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said: 'Tomorrow is a Sabbath rest, a holy Sabbath to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.' So today bake whatever you mean to bake and boil whatever you mean to boil. Put aside everything left over and keep it for the morning."

L.23: And he said to them, "That [is] what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has spoken: 'A Sabbath rest, a holy Sabbath to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [is] tomorrow.' What you will bake, bake, and what you will boil, boil, and all the surplus lay aside for yourselves to be kept until the morning."

R.23: Moses told them, "This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said: 'Tomorrow is a day of rest, a holy Sabbath day for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.' So today, bake and boil all you want. Save what is left over until the next morning."

decisions.choice: a Sabbath rest, a holy Sabbath to Yahweh: the first mention of the Sabbath in Exodus
decisions.reason: This is the first time the Sabbath is named in the Bible. The words come from a root meaning to stop or rest; the first word is a stronger form, a day of complete rest (31:15; Leviticus 23:3). The day is holy, set apart, and it belongs to Yahweh. God rested on the seventh day at creation (Genesis 2:2-3), and here, before the law at Sinai (20:8-11), he teaches Israel to keep the day by the way he gives the manna.

decisions.choice: what you will bake, bake: cook today what you need
decisions.reason: The manna could be baked or boiled (Numbers 11:8). The people are to cook today what they want, and keep the rest uncooked or cooked for the Sabbath.

decisions.choice: Yahweh's words: the announcement of the Sabbath
alternatives: Yahweh's words run to the end of the verse
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has no quotation marks. Yahweh's words may be only the announcement that tomorrow is a Sabbath, with the instructions that follow given by Moses, or they may include the instructions as well. Either way the instructions come from God's command.

decisions.choice: a day of rest ... Sabbath day
decisions.reason: Readable explains the word Sabbath as "a day of rest" the first time it appears.

records.source: וַיַּנִּ֤יחוּ אֹתוֹ֙ עַד־הַבֹּ֔קֶר כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר צִוָּ֣ה מֹשֶׁ֑ה וְלֹ֣א הִבְאִ֔ישׁ וְרִמָּ֖ה לֹא־הָ֥יְתָה בּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And they left it until the morning, just as had commanded Moses, and not it stank, and a maggot not was in it.
pieces: They set it aside until morning, just as Moses had ordered. It did not start to smell, and no maggots appeared in it.

L.24: And they laid it aside until the morning, just as Moses had commanded, and it did not stink, and there was no maggot in it.

R.24: So they saved it until morning, as Moses had told them. It did not smell bad, and there were no worms in it.

decisions.choice: it did not stink: kept by God for the Sabbath
decisions.reason: Manna kept overnight on other days rotted (verse 20). Kept for the Sabbath, it stayed fresh. The difference shows God's hand, not the nature of the food.

decisions.choice: maggot: a different word from the worms of verse 20
decisions.reason: This word means a maggot or grub, the larva that breeds in rotting food (Job 25:6). The meaning is close to "worms" in verse 20.

records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר מֹשֶׁה֙ אִכְלֻ֣הוּ הַיּ֔וֹם כִּֽי־שַׁבָּ֥ת הַיּ֖וֹם לַיהוָ֑ה הַיּ֕וֹם לֹ֥א תִמְצָאֻ֖הוּ בַּשָּׂדֶֽה׃
records.gloss: And said Moses, eat it today, for a sabbath today [is] to Yahweh; today not you will find it in the field.
pieces: Moses said, "Today, eat this. Today is a Sabbath to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; you will find none of it out in the field today.

L.25: And Moses said, "Eat it today, for today [is] a Sabbath to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; today you will not find it in the field.

R.25: Moses said, "Eat this food today. Today is the Sabbath day of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. You will not find any of it out in the fields today.

decisions.choice: a Sabbath to Yahweh: a day of rest belonging to Yahweh
decisions.reason: "To Yahweh" means for him, belonging to him, as in verse 23.

decisions.choice: the field: open country outside the camp
decisions.reason: The field is the open ground where the manna lay, around the camp (verses 13-14).

records.source: שֵׁ֥שֶׁת יָמִ֖ים תִּלְקְטֻ֑הוּ וּבַיּ֧וֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִ֛י שַׁבָּ֖ת לֹ֥א יִֽהְיֶה־בּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: Six days you will gather it, and on the seventh day [is] a sabbath; not will be in it.
pieces: For six days you are to gather it. But the seventh day is a Sabbath, and on it there will be nothing to gather."

L.26: Six days you shall gather it, but on the seventh day [is] a Sabbath; there will be none on it."

R.26: You will gather it for six days. But the seventh day is the Sabbath, and there will be none on that day."

decisions.choice: six days ... the seventh day a Sabbath: the pattern of creation
decisions.reason: Six days of work and a seventh of rest follow the pattern of creation (Genesis 2:2-3), the pattern the fourth commandment gives (20:9-11).

records.source: וַֽיְהִי֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִ֔י יָצְא֥וּ מִן־הָעָ֖ם לִלְקֹ֑ט וְלֹ֖א מָצָֽאוּ׃ס
records.gloss: And it was on the seventh day, went out some of the people to gather, and not they found.
pieces: Even so, when the seventh day came, some of the people went out to gather it, and they found nothing.

L.27: And it came about on the seventh day [that some] of the people went out to gather, and they did not find [any].

R.27: On the seventh day some people went out to look for it anyway, but they did not find any.

decisions.choice: some went out to gather: the test of verse 4 again
decisions.reason: As in verse 20, some of the people did not trust Moses' word and went to see for themselves. God's next words (verse 28) treat this as a refusal to keep his commands.

decisions.choice: Even so / anyway
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable bring out that the people went against what Moses had said in verses 25-26.

records.source: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֑ה עַד־אָ֨נָה֙ מֵֽאַנְתֶּ֔ם לִשְׁמֹ֥ר מִצְוֺתַ֖י וְתוֹרֹתָֽי׃
records.gloss: And said Yahweh to Moses, until when have you refused to keep my commandments and my laws?
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "How long will you people go on refusing to keep {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} commandments and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} laws?

L.28: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Until when do you refuse to keep {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} commandments and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} laws?

R.28: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "How long will you people refuse to obey {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} commands and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} laws?

decisions.choice: you: the people, spoken to through Moses
decisions.reason: "You" is plural. God speaks to Moses, but the rebuke is for the people, who will hear it from him; Moses himself had not gone out.

decisions.choice: until when: how long
decisions.reason: The question is a rebuke, not a request for a date. God used the same question of Pharaoh in 10:3.

decisions.choice: my commandments and my laws: everything God has told them
decisions.reason: The two words together mean all of God's instruction. Here that includes the rules about the manna and the Sabbath (verses 4, 16, 19, 23).

decisions.choice: you people
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "you people" to show that "you" is plural, the people and not Moses alone.

records.heading: Sabbath rest and the jar of manna

records.source: רְא֗וּ כִּֽי־יְהוָה֮ נָתַ֣ן לָכֶ֣ם הַשַּׁבָּת֒ עַל־כֵּ֠ן ה֣וּא נֹתֵ֥ן לָכֶ֛ם בַּיּ֥וֹם הַשִּׁשִּׁ֖י לֶ֣חֶם יוֹמָ֑יִם שְׁב֣וּ׀אִ֣ישׁ תַּחְתָּ֗יו אַל־יֵ֥צֵא אִ֛ישׁ מִמְּקֹמ֖וֹ בַּיּ֥וֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִֽי׃
records.gloss: See that Yahweh has given to you the sabbath; therefore he [is] giving to you on the sixth day bread of two days. Remain each in his place; not let go out anyone from his place on the seventh day.
pieces: Understand this: {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has given you the Sabbath. That is why on the sixth day {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} provides you with bread for two days. On the seventh day all of you are to stay where you are; no one is to leave home."

L.29: See, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has given you the Sabbath; therefore on the sixth day {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gives you bread for two days. Remain {{gender:each one|each man}} in {{gender:their|his}} place; let no one go out from {{gender:their|his}} place on the seventh day."

R.29: Remember that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has given you the Sabbath. That is why {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gives you enough food for two days on the sixth day. On the seventh day, everyone must stay home. No one should go out."

decisions.choice: Yahweh has given you the Sabbath: the day of rest is a gift
decisions.reason: The Sabbath is described as a gift to Israel, not only a demand. God gives it, and gives the food that makes it possible to rest (compare Mark 2:27).

decisions.choice: remain in his place: stay at home, in the camp
decisions.reason: The command is not to go out to gather (verse 27). "His place" is where each one lives in the camp. Later Jewish practice built on this verse the limit of a "Sabbath day's walk" (Acts 1:12).

decisions.choice: see: take note, understand
decisions.reason: "See" here means "consider" or "understand"; it calls the people to grasp the reason for the double portion.

records.source: וַיִּשְׁבְּת֥וּ הָעָ֖ם בַּיּ֥וֹם הַשְּׁבִעִֽי׃
records.gloss: And rested the people on the seventh day.
pieces: So on the seventh day the people rested.

L.30: And the people rested on the seventh day.

R.30: So on the seventh day, the people rested.

decisions.choice: rested: stopped work, kept Sabbath
decisions.reason: The verb comes from the same root as "Sabbath": to stop or cease. The people kept the first Sabbath by stopping their gathering.

records.source: וַיִּקְרְא֧וּ בֵֽית־יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל אֶת־שְׁמ֖וֹ מָ֑ן וְה֗וּא כְּזֶ֤רַע גַּד֙ לָבָ֔ן וְטַעְמ֖וֹ כְּצַפִּיחִ֥ת בִּדְבָֽשׁ׃
records.gloss: And called [the] house of Israel its name manna; and it [was] like seed of coriander, white, and its taste [was] like a wafer with honey.
pieces: The people of Israel named it manna. It was like coriander seed, but white, and its taste was like honey wafers.

L.31: And the house of Israel called its name manna; and it [was] like coriander seed, white, and its taste [was] like a wafer with honey.

R.31: The Israelites called the food manna. It was white and looked like small coriander seeds. It tasted like thin cakes made with honey.

decisions.choice: manna: the name recalls the question "What is it?"
decisions.reason: The name sounds like the question the people asked when they first saw it (verse 15). See the note there.

decisions.choice: like coriander seed, white: small and round, but white
decisions.reason: Coriander seed is small, round and grayish-brown, so the likeness is in size and shape; the manna was white. Numbers 11:7 adds that it looked like bdellium, a pale resin.

decisions.choice: a wafer with honey: a thin cake sweetened with honey
decisions.reason: The word for wafer occurs only here; it means a thin, flat cake. Numbers 11:8 compares the taste of manna cooked in pans to cakes made with oil.

decisions.choice: the people of Israel / the Israelites
decisions.reason: "The house of Israel" means the whole nation. Literal keeps "house".

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֗ה זֶ֤ה הַדָּבָר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר צִוָּ֣ה יְהוָ֔ה מְלֹ֤א הָעֹ֨מֶר֙ מִמֶּ֔נּוּ לְמִשְׁמֶ֖רֶת לְדֹרֹתֵיכֶ֑ם לְמַ֣עַן׀יִרְא֣וּ אֶת־הַלֶּ֗חֶם אֲשֶׁ֨ר הֶאֱכַ֤לְתִּי אֶתְכֶם֙ בַּמִּדְבָּ֔ר בְּהוֹצִיאִ֥י אֶתְכֶ֖ם מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: And said Moses, this [is] the word that has commanded Yahweh: [the] fullness of the omer of it [is] for keeping for your generations, so that they may see the bread that I fed you in the wilderness when I brought out you from [the] land of Egypt.
pieces: Moses said, "Here is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has commanded: 'Set aside {{units:a full 2 quarts|a full omer}} of it to be kept for your descendants, generation after generation. Then they can look at the bread I gave you to eat in the wilderness after I brought you out of Egypt.'"

L.32: And Moses said, "This [is] the thing that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has commanded: 'An omer full of it [is] to be kept for your generations, so that they may see the bread that I fed you in the wilderness when I brought you out from the land of Egypt.'"

R.32: Moses said, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has given this command: 'Keep {{units:2 quarts|an omer}} of manna for your children and grandchildren and all who come after them. Then they will see the food I gave you in the desert when I brought you out of Egypt.'"

decisions.choice: for keeping for your generations: to be kept for all time
decisions.reason: "For your generations" means for every generation to come (12:14, 17). The jar of manna was a witness to God's care in the wilderness.

decisions.choice: I fed you: God speaks in his own voice
decisions.reason: Moses quotes God's command, so "I" is God. He fed Israel with the manna as a parent feeds a child (Deuteronomy 8:3, 16).

decisions.choice: {{units:a full 2 quarts|a full omer}}
decisions.reason: As in verse 16, the modern measure comes first, with the omer as the alternative. Literal keeps "omer".

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֜ה אֶֽל־אַהֲרֹ֗ן קַ֚ח צִנְצֶ֣נֶת אַחַ֔ת וְתֶן־שָׁ֥מָּה מְלֹֽא־הָעֹ֖מֶר מָ֑ן וְהַנַּ֤ח אֹתוֹ֙ לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה לְמִשְׁמֶ֖רֶת לְדֹרֹתֵיכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And said Moses to Aaron, take one jar and put there [the] fullness of the omer of manna, and place it before Yahweh for keeping for your generations.
pieces: Moses told Aaron, "Get a jar and put {{units:a full 2 quarts|a full omer}} of manna into it. Then set it in the presence of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, to be kept for all your generations to come."

L.33: And Moses said to Aaron, "Take one jar and put in it an omer full of manna, and place it before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to be kept for your generations."

R.33: Moses told Aaron, "Get a jar and put {{units:2 quarts|an omer}} of manna in it. Then place it in front of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. It must be kept there for all your children and grandchildren and the people who come after them."

decisions.choice: jar: a container, probably of clay or metal
decisions.reason: The word occurs only here. Hebrews 9:4 calls it a golden jar kept in the ark.

decisions.choice: before Yahweh: in the place of God's presence
decisions.reason: To place something before Yahweh is to put it where God is present to his people, later the tabernacle, in front of the ark (verse 34).

records.source: כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר צִוָּ֥ה יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֑ה וַיַּנִּיחֵ֧הוּ אַהֲרֹ֛ן לִפְנֵ֥י הָעֵדֻ֖ת לְמִשְׁמָֽרֶת׃
records.gloss: Just as had commanded Yahweh to Moses, and placed it Aaron before the testimony for keeping.
pieces: Aaron set it in front of the testimony for safekeeping, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had told Moses to do.

L.34: Just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded Moses, Aaron placed it before the testimony, to be kept.

R.34: Aaron did what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded Moses. He put the jar of manna in front of the covenant tablets so that it would be kept safe.

decisions.choice: the testimony: the tablets of the covenant
decisions.reason: "The testimony" is the name for the two stone tablets of the covenant law, the witness to God's covenant with Israel (25:16, 21; 31:18). They were kept in the ark, called "the ark of the testimony" (25:22).

decisions.choice: before the testimony: written from a later point in the story
decisions.reason: The tablets and the ark are not given until Sinai (chapters 24-25 and 40:20). The narrator tells here what was done with the jar once there was a testimony to put it before, completing the account of the manna in one place, as verse 35 also does.

decisions.choice: the covenant tablets
decisions.reason: Readable explains "the testimony" as the covenant tablets; Literal and Balanced keep "testimony".

records.source: וּבְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל אָֽכְל֤וּ אֶת־הַמָּן֙ אַרְבָּעִ֣ים שָׁנָ֔ה עַד־בֹּאָ֖ם אֶל־אֶ֣רֶץ נוֹשָׁ֑בֶת אֶת־הַמָּן֙ אָֽכְל֔וּ עַד־בֹּאָ֕ם אֶל־קְצֵ֖ה אֶ֥רֶץ כְּנָֽעַן׃
records.gloss: And [the] sons of Israel ate the manna forty years, until they came to a land inhabited; the manna they ate until they came to [the] border of [the] land of Canaan.
pieces: For forty years the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} ate manna, until they reached a land where people lived. They went on eating manna until they arrived at the edge of the land of Canaan.

L.35: And the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel ate the manna forty years, until they came to an inhabited land; they ate the manna until they came to the border of the land of Canaan.

R.35: The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} ate manna for forty years, until they came to a land where people lived. They ate manna until they came to the edge of Canaan.

decisions.choice: forty years, until the border of Canaan: the manna lasted all through the wilderness
decisions.reason: The narrator looks ahead to the end of the wilderness years (Numbers 14:33-34). The manna stopped the day after Israel ate the produce of Canaan at Gilgal (Joshua 5:10-12).

decisions.choice: an inhabited land ... the border of Canaan: the same end, said twice
decisions.reason: The two clauses describe the same point from two sides: the end of the uninhabited wilderness, at the edge of Canaan.

records.source: וְהָעֹ֕מֶר עֲשִׂרִ֥ית הָאֵיפָ֖ה הֽוּא׃פ
records.gloss: And the omer, a tenth of the ephah it [is].
pieces: (An omer is {{units:about 2 quarts, one tenth of an ephah|one tenth of an ephah}}.)

L.36: Now the omer is a tenth of the ephah.

R.36: (An omer was a dry measure of {{units:about 2 quarts|one tenth of an ephah}}.)

decisions.choice: the omer is a tenth of the ephah: a note for later readers
decisions.reason: This is an editorial note, not part of the story, explaining the omer of verses 16-33 by a better-known measure. The ephah was the usual dry measure, about half a bushel (roughly 20 quarts), so an omer was about 2 quarts. The note suggests that the omer was no longer a familiar unit when the account was written down.

decisions.choice: {{units:about 2 quarts, one tenth of an ephah|one tenth of an ephah}}
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the modern measure first, with the original definition as the alternative, and set the note in parentheses as an aside. Literal keeps the Hebrew form.
